description:
NOT ACTIONABLE TODAY - kept as a design note. Its premise was bedrock-q67.21.16 (PR #201), which was closed as dead code, so there is no "unreadable" worker state for anything to exit from.

THE SCENARIO ALSO LOOKS UNREACHABLE. Chunks are NEVER deleted (demux/shard_server.ex:324) - Bedrock has no retention floor for shard chunks - so a materializer can always replay its shard's full history from zero. The only path that faked such a gap was a swallowed listing error, fixed at the root by bedrock-q67.21.17.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING:

FDB's answer to a genuinely lost log position is kill-and-rebuild, not refuse-and-linger: "if (cursor->popped() > 0) throw worker_removed()" (storageserver.actor.cpp:12119-12123) followed by persistentData->dispose() (:15001-15005) - the worker exits, its files are deleted, and DD recruits fresh.

The asymmetry that makes worker replacement the right mechanism for US: an FDB storage server hosts MANY shards, so it must refetch in place rather than die over one bad range. A Bedrock materializer serves exactly one shard (State.shard_num/shard_id, singular), so the worker and the shard are the same unit of failure, and FDB's per-shard state machine collapses to a per-worker fact.

The hole is fillable without peer fetch: restoring a snapshot at or above the missing span and resuming the pull closes it exactly. The object-storage snapshot IS Bedrock's fetchKeys, and the startup path already performs it (Logic.maybe_load_snapshot/2). Exiting therefore reuses machinery that exists and is already damped - the distributor's DOWN handling retires the member and re-recruits with per-tag backoff - and the replacement re-runs discovery and restore through ordinary startup. No live database swap.

IF IT EVER BECOMES ACTIONABLE: the exit reason must be distinguishable from the other voluntary exits, because they mean opposite things to the distributor. shutdown/idle means "do not re-recruit, revival is demand-driven" (bedrock-q67.21.5); displacement means "someone else owns this now"; an unreadable exit means "re-recruit promptly, the shard needs coverage". And a replacement that hits the same condition will loop through recruit -> exit -> recruit; the per-tag backoff damps it, but it must READ as a data-availability failure rather than as churn.

REVISIT ONLY IF a retention floor for chunks is introduced, or another mechanism can leave a worker genuinely unable to reconstruct its shard.
title: An unreadable materializer exits so it can be replaced (the snapshot is our fetchKeys)
